thesis: The speakers argue that prediction markets are superior information aggregation mechanisms because they effectively surface dispersed knowledge from millions of people, resulting in predictions that are more accurate than polls or complex statistical models. They explain that this accuracy is driven by the market's ability to embed private estimates and preferences into asset prices, which inherently pushes the market closer to the truth.
